title: Chanel No. 5
blurb: Launched in 1921, the aldehyde-laden floral that became the most famous perfume in the world.

title: Shalimar
blurb: Guerlain's 1925 vanilla-and-bergamot oriental, named after the gardens of a Mughal emperor.

title: Eau de Cologne
blurb: A light citrus fragrance first mixed in Cologne in 1709, meant to smell like an Italian spring morning.

title: Old Spice
blurb: The nautical-themed aftershave in the ivory bottle that generations of grandfathers smelled of.

title: Opium
blurb: Yves Saint Laurent's heady 1977 spice-and-amber scent, as controversial as it was successful.

title: CK One
blurb: The clean citrus fragrance of 1994, sold in a plain flask and worn by everyone regardless of gender.

title: Attar
blurb: A concentrated perfume oil distilled from flowers, herbs or woods into sandalwood, with no alcohol at all.

title: Rose water
blurb: Water scented by steeping or distilling rose petals, used for perfume, sweets and ceremonies for millennia.

title: Incense
blurb: Aromatic resin, wood or paste burned for its fragrant smoke, in sticks, cones and coils.

title: Pomander
blurb: A ball of perfumes, or an orange studded with cloves, once carried to ward off bad air.

title: Potpourri
blurb: A bowl of dried petals, peel and spices that quietly scents a room.

title: Ambergris
blurb: A waxy substance from sperm whales that washes ashore and was long prized for fixing perfume.
